clue.text: Tear up as Spooner might say, looking for understanding …

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the two words found here trade their starts

parts.note: a side that is up in a match is ahead
swapping the opening sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone rips something apart while groping for comprehension, the trailing dots leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the R and L of RIP LEADING to get LIP READING. The ellipsis just links this clue to 6 Across for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading is watching a speaker's mouth to grasp their words, literally looking in order to understand.

clue.text: As it happens, sin is on the rise

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A moralist laments that wrongdoing is increasing even as we speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A live broadcast goes out in real time, as events happen.

clue.text: One may take the lead in war against crime

definitions.text: One may take the lead in war against crime

parts.words: One may take the lead in war against crime
parts.note: surface reading: someone heading the fight against criminals
setter's reading: an animal literally attached to a leash, working for the force

explanation.surface: A campaigner might head up the battle against lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the lead' suggests leadership, but it means being walked on a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained canine used by officers is kept on a leash and helps fight crime.

clue.text: Source of inspiration from reader at Oxford

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of reader and the start of at Oxford

explanation.surface: An academic lecturer at the university inspires students.
explanation.walkthrough: A reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain. Erato is one of the nine Muses, of love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muses were the classical goddesses who inspired poets and artists.

clue.text: Ate about four, as predicted

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the meal word wraps round the numeral

explanation.surface: Someone had dinner at around four o'clock, just as forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foresee by intuition or supernatural insight, so divined means foretold.

clue.text: Star upset about poor clue for centre

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the sun is a star, read upwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom
a poor version is badly formed, so its letters need rearranging

parts.note: rearranged, which here happens to leave it unchanged

explanation.surface: A celebrity is cross about a weak clue in the middle of the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of clue ends up as CLUE itself, a cheeky touch; it goes inside SUN turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the core or central part around which other things gather.

clue.text: … material left after renovation

indicators.note: renovation remakes something, so the word before it gets its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 Across, some fabric remains once a room has been done up.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is a fabric made of matted, pressed wool fibres.

clue.text: Pulls in listeners across north

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the hearing organs straddle the letter

explanation.surface: A radio station attracts an audience across the north of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull in money is to earn it, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Thrills from new games underpinning rising skill

indicators.note: in a down entry, what underpins lies below, so it comes after the other piece
in a down entry a rising word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Fresh sporting events built on growing ability excite the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with strong emotion, so transports means delights.

clue.text: Cloudy and cold when in open

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first two pieces sit within the last

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
as can mean when, e.g. 'as he left'

explanation.surface: The weather is grey and chilly out in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is completely covered by cloud.

clue.text: Some rejected agricultural living accommodation

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the letters run backwards
some means only a portion of the words that follow is taken

parts.note: the end of agricultural and the start of living

explanation.surface: Some farm workers' housing has been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large house, often in the country or abroad, so a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: The other way round since vicar retracted on sin

indicators.note: in an across entry, being on something means following it
retracted means drawn back, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: as can mean since, e.g. 'as it rained'
Rev, short for Reverend, the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: A clergyman took back his statement on wrongdoing, saying the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is Latin for with the positions reversed, i.e. conversely.

clue.text: Sponge rugs once restored

indicators.note: restored means put back together, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to clean carpets that were once renovated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' reads as a noun or a cleaning verb, but it means living off others.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to cadge from others without paying back, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Sprays flowers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: perforated nozzles on watering cans or showers
second meaning: blooms of a familiar thorny garden shrub

explanation.walkthrough: Sprays of flowers is a natural phrase, but each word is a separate definition; a rose is also the sprinkler head of a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the perforated nozzles of watering cans and the classic garden bloom.

clue.text: Surely not fine at home always

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A disbelieving reply to someone claiming to be content to stay indoors forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise and disbelief at something just said.

clue.text: Granted — and due for payment on completion

indicators.note: in an across entry, sitting on something means coming after it

parts.note: money that is owed is due

explanation.surface: A contract term: the sum is awarded and payable once the work is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To be endowed is to be given or provided with money or a quality.

clue.text: Court lacks flexible seating in the Lords

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: something flexible can be bent into another shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judicial chamber is short of adaptable chairs in the upper house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Woolsack is the wool-stuffed cushion on which the Lord Speaker sits in the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Woolsack is the official seat of the presiding officer in the House of Lords.

clue.text: A politician blocking leave for cleaner

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: shoo! is a command to go away

explanation.surface: An MP stands in the way of someone's leave request for a janitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap used for washing hair or carpets.

clue.text: What Siberia would be if not south?

definitions.text: What Siberia would be if not south?

parts.words: What Siberia would be if not south?
parts.note: surface reading: a geography question about the frozen region of Russia moved elsewhere
setter's reading: remove the S, the abbreviation for south, and Siberia becomes Iberia, the land of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what the frozen Russian region would be if it were not in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Siberia is not actually southern, which signals a letter trick: drop S and you get Iberia, which is almost surrounded by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian landmass is a piece of land projecting into the sea, joined to the mainland on one side.

clue.text: Thousands may find no resistance in shackles

indicators.note: no here means without, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: chains for the legs of prisoners
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Thousands of prisoners in chains offer no resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Legions are vast numbers, from the Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers.

clue.text: Fantastic rates adjusted to cover lines

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged
covering something means going around it, so the rearranged word wraps the other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Excellent prices have been tweaked to include extra rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar, literally starry, is used informally to mean outstanding or brilliant.

clue.text: Former money court that is no longer

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A one-time cash tribunal has been abolished.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct species or thing no longer exists, having died out.

clue.text: Words after passing on the app I devised

indicators.note: devised means invented or put together, so the letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: Messages left after a death are hosted on a smartphone program I created.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing on' reads as one phrase about death, but 'on' is just a link and 'passing' alone means dying.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is an inscription or tribute written about someone who has died.

clue.text: Creatures seeing terror initially in all directions

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the other piece
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Animals spot something frightening and scatter every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts are small amphibians, so they are animals.

clue.text: Best beat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to get the better of

explanation.walkthrough: Best looks like a superlative and the answer looks like its opposite, but both clue words are verbs meaning defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to worst an opponent is to defeat them, so it matches both to best and to beat.

clue.text: Issues resulting from cycling rebellion

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the first letter moves round to the end

explanation.surface: Problems arise from an uprising, or from a bike protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Editions of a newspaper or magazine are its issues, a synonym.

clue.text: Feeling others must expose bar

indicators.note: exposing reveals something already there, so the letters are found within the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A sense that other people ought to reveal the drinking establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, typically gold.

clue.text: A short note added to end of the recess

parts.note: PS, short for postscript, a note added at the end of a letter

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A brief memo is appended to the tail end of the break period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' suggests a school or parliamentary break, but it is the architectural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Disease of 10 Across treated with care

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the combined letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An illness at a country house is looked after with tenderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' fits the medical surface perfectly, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Varicella is the medical name for chickenpox.

clue.text: President losing time for golf is a misery guts

indicators.note: losing one thing for another means swapping it out, so one letter is replaced

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A president who gives up time for golf is a sourpuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Misery guts is British slang for a perpetually gloomy, complaining person.
explanation.definitionFit: A grump is a bad-tempered, moaning person, the same sort as a misery guts.

clue.text: Ceremony that's correct for the audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: correct is right, said out loud

explanation.surface: A ritual performed properly in front of the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or solemn act, a ritual.

clue.text: Frame principal Italian party

parts.note: arch- as in archenemy means chief
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
a rave is a lively party

explanation.surface: Someone sets up the main Italian political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' reads as a verb about framing someone, but it is the noun for a moulding.
explanation.definitionFit: An architrave is the moulded frame surrounding a door or window.
